reasons.reader_question: The chapter closes on a specific, well-earned question. Ittan's 'Hands go where they're sent' plus 'whose palm was open' points beyond him. Readers who caught the green-wax gift may already half-guess the queen, so the curiosity runs at intermediate rather than peak confidence.
reasons.change: Several things are concrete and irreversible by the end. Ammu is buried and Neela is rogue with no master and only a thumb of stolen resin. The cages stay shut, and the bodies are bound. Devan now holds clove-and-wax evidence and has openly pressed Ittan.
reasons.romance_movement: The relationship changes for new reasons. Wound-share binds them in body. He says Ammu's name back to her. 'I'd like it to have someone who is' turns grief into household, matching the beat's 'each other's only household'.
reasons.shown_chemistry: Chemistry is shown through responsive action, not narration. He binds her wrists with his teeth and jokes 'Then I'll bleed in pairs.' He waits on the step with 'I'll be here.' He orders the fodder run that answers her promise. Her knee comes to rest against the bay's flank and his hand uncurls.
reasons.character_logic: Mostly smart, with three lapses. Neela reacts to the wound-share as a fresh discovery, though Ammu told her an hour earlier and she recognised it in ch 27. She claims 'the only people on earth' who know her are Muthu and Devan, while Chathu, Vellan and the hunters all know. Her hands 'would not close', yet she does heavy well and fodder work with no wound-share echo on Devan.
reasons.stakes_and_cost: Each decision carries a cost. Leaving the cages shut is a real moral price. The resin is framed as a debt. Keeping Muthu at the gate and letting Ittan sleep unsearched are both risks that carry into the sealing.
reasons.prose: Clean and concrete, with no banned phrases and few AI tells. The kennel passage states the no-undo rule three times in a row. 'Did not' openings pile up, and the 'Is that mine?' / 'It's mine' / 'It's yours' exchange reads as confusion rather than intent.
reasons.continuity: The line 'When you split it on Vellan I felt it, and I thought it was the bear' contradicts ch 27 and F340. There, Neela in shape recognises the tearing at once as the wound-share Ammu described ('A cut on him opens on you'). The fodder-run order (F342) also sits badly with F289/F291, where the first run was held by rain.

fixes: At 'When you split it on Vellan I felt it, and I thought it was the bear', there is a continuity break with ch 27/F340 and a smart heroine forgetting what Ammu told her an hour ago (irrational behaviour). Rewrite so she already knew the rule and is shaken by its reality instead. For example: 'Ammu told me. A cut on you opens on me. She didn't say it would feel like this.' Keep 'For the rest of my life, Devan' as the turn. Untangle the 'Is that mine?' / 'It's mine' exchange so each line has one clear meaning: he asks whether the welt is his wound, and she answers 'It's yours. On me.'

At 'Bhaskaran's men go out the morning after we're home', this conflicts with F289/F291, where the first fodder run is held by rain. Make the order conditional: 'The first cart goes as soon as the wood road will take a wheel. Then every week the roads allow.' Revise F342 so the run is due within three days but may be held by rain, which keeps ch 31 intact.

At 'The only people on earth who knew what she was', there is a logic error, because Chathu, Vellan and every Resin House hunter know. Change it to 'The only people on her side of any wall who knew what she was'. Also cut the redundant 'Opening the doors would not end their caging.' The paragraph already says 'A cage could be unlocked. A caging could not.'
reader_question: If Ittan is only a hand sent by someone else, whose hand is he?
new_facts_assessment: F342 (Bhaskaran's four men leave the morning after the return; Muthu kept 'at the gate') has two good effects. It makes leaving the kennels bearable, and it keeps Muthu in place for the ch 29 search, which suits Devan's suspicion (F217, F222). However, it conflicts with F289/F291, which say the first Resin House run was held by rain and Muthu carried it in three days. One of the two must change; the dialogue can absorb the rain hold. F343 (Neela on the west rampart where the pulled sentry stood) is consistent with F064, F077 and F079 and is harmless. The new claim that this stretch of wall bends toward the padippura is fine, since the gate's position is not fixed elsewhere. Two unlisted additions also need judging. Ammu's Valli cloth was cached at the tree roots 'before dusk', which is plausible only if she slipped out before being posted to the kennel, so it is minor. Ittan's clove-oil wife's-cough cover and his clerk with tallies agree with F259 and F263 and are well used as a clue at the peak.
